solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Whisky and wine consumed inside did harm

parts.note: malt is a kind of whisky

indicators.note: inside tells us the word for consumed sits within the wine word

parts.note: red is wine of that colour
to consume food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone's drinking session of whisky and wine did them damage.
explanation.definitionFit: To maltreat is to treat badly or abuse, so maltreated is a past-tense equivalent of did harm.

clue.text: Blood there is missing — litres pumped in?

indicators.note: something pumped in is forced inside another thing

parts.note: caret is Latin for 'there is missing', and names the proofreader's mark showing an omission
L is the abbreviation for litres

explanation.surface: A medical scene: blood is missing, so is it being pumped back in by the litre?
explanation.walkthrough: The proofreader's mark ^ is called a caret because the Latin word means 'there is missing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is British slang, chiefly in boxing and football, for blood, from the dark red colour of the wine.

clue.text: Mayhem: split cyst disrupted biological network

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical drama: a split cyst causes mayhem inside the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the letters to be rearranged; 'disrupted' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: The lymphatic system is the body's web of vessels and nodes carrying lymph, a network in biology.

clue.text: Trio never in harmony relentless with simple instrument

parts.note: something eternal never lets up
the triangle is a basic percussion instrument

explanation.surface: A musical trio who can never agree, stuck with a relentless player of a basic instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface hides a romantic definition: the trio is not a band but three people.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternal triangle is a love affair involving three people, such as a married couple and a lover, which is rarely harmonious.

clue.text: Upright character deserting Mail — City's explosive secret?

indicators.note: something explosive is blown apart, so its letters scatter into a new order
deserting means leaving, so that character drops out of the following words

parts.note: the letter I is a single upright stroke
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A newspaper story: a key figure leaves the Daily Mail, revealing an explosive City secret.
explanation.walkthrough: One I is removed from MAIL CITYS and the remaining eight letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystical means having a hidden or esoteric meaning, so it can describe something secret.

clue.text: Trump slogan in first publication?

parts.note: mag is short for magazine
A is the first letter, the first of a series as in plan A

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Trump slogan made its debut in print.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'first publication' as magazine A, the first of a series, with the letter after the noun as in plan A.
explanation.definitionFit: MAGA is the initialism of Make America Great Again, Donald Trump's campaign slogan.

clue.text: Why in fairy tale most disturbed chap offers line from 19?

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the preceding words lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A troubled man in a fairy tale asks why, quoting Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: The 19 refers to the answer at 19 down, the play. The rearranged letters supply all but the last three, which the chap adds unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet speaks this famous line in Act 1, scene 2, deploring his mother's hasty remarriage.

clue.text: Soldiers turned up stopping endless film prank

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, sitting inside it
endless means losing its final letter

parts.note: a flick is a film

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops arrive to halt a film shoot that never ends, as a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A frolic is a playful escapade or bit of fun, close in sense to a prank.

clue.text: See 7
Send overseas from harbour once?

parts.note: ex means former, what once was
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: Shipping goods abroad from what used to be a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'from harbour once' is a playful way of saying a harbour that used to be one.
explanation.definitionFit: To export is to ship goods to another country for sale.

clue.text: More from Scots in West perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Scottish word for more
second meaning: a first name found in a famous Hollywood star's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'West' is not a direction but the surname of the actress Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: Mae is Scots dialect for more, and Mae is the given name of the film star Mae West.

clue.text: Flowering spuds perhaps emerge from soil

parts.note: a plant in flower is said to be out
potatoes are an example of a crop

explanation.surface: Potato plants in bloom pushing up out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Spuds are potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, outcrop means of rock, to appear at the surface of the ground.

clue.text: See 24
Lively celebration eschews any extreme language

indicators.note: eschewing both extremes means dropping the very first and very last letters

parts.note: a shindig is a lively party

explanation.surface: A party that steers clear of extremes in any form.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is the main official language of India.

clue.text: Arnie out to cover return of mating sloth

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
covering something means wrapping around it
out here means disordered, so the name's letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
it is a slang word for sex

explanation.surface: Arnie goes out, perhaps to film animals mating, though sloths are slow at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' is not the animal but the sin of laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to do nothing, a synonym for sloth in the sense of idleness.

clue.text: Cones around this vehicle news boss opens?

indicators.note: here the boss breaks the vehicle open by getting inside it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Traffic cones placed around a car that a newspaper editor is opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The traffic cones are really the cones of a conifer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar is a conifer bearing woody cones, so cones are found around this tree.

clue.text: Duke, warlord playing with me in fantasy situation

indicators.note: playing about with something rearranges it freely

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Duke
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A duke and a warlord play games with the speaker in some fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream-world is an unrealistic imagined state, a fantasy situation in which someone lives.

clue.text: Ace report in story on ticket: fare from Bologna

indicators.note: in places the ace and report within the story word

parts.note: a tag is a label or ticket
a story can be a lie
A is the card abbreviation for ace
to tell is to report

explanation.surface: Reporting an ace in a story placed on a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in an across clue puts the story part after the ticket part.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagliatelle is ribbon pasta, a classic dish of Bologna served with ragù.

clue.text: Become obscene entertaining right drama queen?

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, holding them inside

parts.note: to get rude is to become obscene
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A diva turns crude while performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama queen' suggests a showy person, but it is a queen in a play: Hamlet's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude is the queen of Denmark in Shakespeare's Hamlet, literally a queen in a drama.

clue.text: Before noon 50 coming into the stricken village

indicators.note: coming into places the first pieces inside the next
something stricken is battered out of shape, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
am stands for ante meridiem, before midday
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Fifty people arrive in a disaster-hit village one morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small village.

clue.text: Releasing uranium, home visitor's put away

indicators.note: releasing means letting go, so that letter drops out

parts.note: at home means in
a guest is a visitor
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A houseguest is jailed after releasing radioactive material.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To put food away is informal for eating it, which is what ingest means.

clue.text: Tree more bare with bark initially removed

indicators.note: initially removed means the starting letter of the following word is taken away

parts.note: balder means more bare
the opening letter of bark

explanation.surface: A tree left more bare after its bark is stripped.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family often growing by water.

clue.text: See 7
Wartime's no time for building German city

indicators.note: building suggests constructing something new out of the letters
no time says the letter for time is not wanted

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: During war there is no time to construct anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Wartime's means 'wartime has', so 'no time' acts on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Weimar is a city in Thuringia, Germany, famous for Goethe and the post-war Weimar Republic.

clue.text: What partly influenced famed US choreographer?

indicators.note: influenced means acted upon and altered, so the letters are changed in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks what partly shaped a celebrated American dancemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' looks like a hidden-word signal, but it is part of the fodder for rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Twyla Tharp is an American dancer and choreographer known for Push Comes to Shove and Movin' Out.

clue.text: Cow perhaps to look sullen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that lows, i.e. moos
second meaning: to frown or scowl, a variant spelling of lour

explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as one that lows, so it rhymes with 'mower'; the second is pronounced to rhyme with 'flower'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow is an example of an animal that moos, and to lower is to scowl or appear gloomy.

clue.text: Like 18 according to 19 in 7-day period, do we hear?

indicators.note: asking what we hear points to a word that sounds like the period named

parts.note: a week is seven days

explanation.surface: Cross-references read as a quiz on a Shakespeare quote and a week.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is Gertrude and 19 is the play; Hamlet's line at 7 calls women frail, so Gertrude is weak in his view.
explanation.definitionFit: Frailty means weakness, so Hamlet's 'Frailty, thy name is woman' casts his mother as weak.

clue.text: No-one's house in Albert Square offensive

indicators.note: Albert Square is the setting of the London soap EastEnders, whose Cockney speech drops the initial h

parts.note: no plus I (one) plus 's
a house is a home

explanation.surface: An empty house on the EastEnders square is seen as unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap set in East London; a Cockney says 'ome for home. 'One' becomes I, the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul-smelling or highly disagreeable, so it serves as offensive.

clue.text: Eviscerate going around tower

indicators.note: going around means turning back to face the other way

parts.note: to gut is to remove the innards

explanation.surface: Disembowelling someone and then circling a tall building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' is not a tall building but something that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a boat that tows ships, literally a tower.

clue.text: Nonsense tango with side-to-side movement

parts.note: tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a waddle is a rocking side-to-side walk

explanation.surface: Dismissing a tango that only wobbles from side to side as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is trivial or foolish talk, a synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Tract in grassland left after ploughing

parts.note: a lea is a meadow

indicators.note: ploughing turns soil over, so the letters it acts on are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tract of meadow left over after the plough has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' looks like a stretch of land, fitting the farm picture, but it is a pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet on a topic, as is a leaflet.
